questions.scenario: A particle is projected from a point O on a horizontal plane with initial velocity u ms^-1 at an angle of 45 degrees to the horizontal. The height h(t) of the particle above the plane after t seconds is given by h(t) = 10t - 5t^2.
questions.question: Calculate the time at which the particle reaches its maximum height.
marking_criteria: Correct differentiation of the height equation
Setting the derivative equal to zero
Solving for t
hints: Stay focused on this: Calculate the time at which the particle reaches its maximum height — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Correct differentiation of the height; the derivative equal to zero; Solving for t.
questions.model_answer: The height equation is h(t) = 10t - 5t^2. Differentiating with respect to t gives h'(t) = 10 - 10t. Setting h'(t) = 0 gives 10 - 10t = 0, so t = 1 second.
questions.explanation: The maximum height is reached when the derivative of the height with respect to time is zero.

questions.scenario: A projectile is launched with an initial velocity of 20 ms^-1 at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal. The height h(t) of the projectile above the ground after t seconds is given by h(t) = 10t - 5t^2.
questions.question: Calculate the time at which the projectile hits the ground.
marking_criteria: Setting h(t) = 0
Solving the quadratic equation
Choosing the correct root
hints: Set the height equation equal to zero and solve for t.
questions.model_answer: Setting h(t) = 0 gives 10t - 5t^2 = 0. Factoring out 5t gives 5t(2 - t) = 0. So, t = 0 or t = 2. Since t = 0 is the launch time, the projectile hits the ground at t = 2 seconds.
questions.explanation: The projectile hits the ground when its height is zero.

questions.scenario: A ball is thrown from a height of 5 metres above the ground with an initial velocity of 15 ms^-1 at an angle of 60 degrees to the horizontal. The height h(t) of the ball above the ground after t seconds is given by h(t) = 5 + 10t - 5t^2.
questions.question: Calculate the time at which the ball hits the ground.
marking_criteria: Setting h(t) = 0
Solving the quadratic equation
Choosing the correct root
hints: Set the height equation equal to zero and solve for t.
questions.model_answer: Setting h(t) = 0 gives 5 + 10t - 5t^2 = 0. Rearranging gives 5t^2 - 10t - 5 = 0. Dividing by 5 gives t^2 - 2t - 1 = 0. Solving this quadratic equation using the quadratic formula gives t = 1 ± sqrt(2). Since time cannot be negative, t = 1 + sqrt(2) seconds.
questions.explanation: The ball hits the ground when its height is zero.
questions.topic_label: The Cartesian equation of the trajectory (Projectiles)

questions.scenario: A projectile is launched from a height of 1 metre above the ground with an initial velocity of 15 m/s at an angle of 45 degrees to the horizontal.
questions.question: Calculate the range of the projectile on the horizontal plane.
marking_criteria: Correct application of the horizontal motion equation
Correct use of trigonometric functions
Correct calculation of range
hints: Stay focused on this: Calculate the range of the projectile on the horizontal plane — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Correct application of the horizontal motion equation; Correct use of trigonometric functions; Correct calculation of range.
questions.model_answer: The horizontal component of the initial velocity is given by 15 * cos(45) = 10.6 m/s. The range is given by R = u_x * t, where t is the total time of flight. The total time of flight is given by 2u_y/g, where u_y = 15 * sin(45) = 10.6 m/s and g = 9.8 m/s^2. Therefore, t = 2 * 10.6 / 9.8 = 2.16 seconds. Hence, R = 10.6 * 2.16 = 22.896 meters.
questions.explanation: The horizontal range of the projectile can be found by multiplying the horizontal component of the initial velocity by the total time of flight. The time of flight is determined by the vertical component of the motion.
